page: Microsoft Azure E4-2ads_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the EADSv5 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an AMD EPYC 7763 processor with x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The instance is configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs, derived from 1 physical core with 2 threads per core. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 16.0 GB per core. Local storage is bundled with a 154 GB local disk, and the server is Premium Storage capable. No GPU accelerators or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included.

Benchmark data reveals a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. The server achieves a strong single-core CPU performance score of 2696.08 in stress-ng, placing it in the top 25%. However, its multi-core CPU performance in the same test is weak, falling into the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth is a notable bottleneck, with read-only small block cached bandwidth measured at 128.11 GB/sec (bottom 10%) and large block uncached read/write speeds scoring in the bottom 25%. Similarly, Geekbench multi-core, software compilation, and ray tracing benchmarks all rank in the bottom 10%, reflecting the limitations of the 2-vCPU allocation for parallelized tasks.

Given its high memory density relative to processing power, the E4-2ads_v5 offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound workloads that do not require intense parallel computation. Single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and bzip3 decompression perform at average levels (middle 50%). However, database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput all register in the bottom 10%, indicating this instance is poorly suited for high-throughput transactional databases or heavy web traffic. It is best utilized for memory-heavy, low-concurrency applications, lightweight caching, or single-threaded data processing tasks.
